uncited: This method extends GPU-based Projected Tetrahedra by pre-computing volume rendering integrals into texture maps, enabling hardware-accelerated compositing of semi-transparent triangles.

It solves the limitation of standard projected tetrahedra by supporting arbitrary transfer functions via pre-integration, at the cost of increased memory usage for 3D textures or approximation errors for 2D textures.

It differs from [Sorted Rasterization of Projected Tetrahedra](3018-sorted-rasterization-of-projected-tetrahedra.md) by relying on texture-based integral approximation rather than explicit sorting of all triangles, and from [On-the-fly Shell Geometry Construction](13927-on-the-fly-shell-geometry-construction.md) by using pre-computed textures instead of dynamic geometry generation.
**Inputs:** A volume dataset, a transfer function, and a viewing direction.
**3D Texture Map (Optional/Original):** Stores pre-integrated color and opacity.
Dimensions correspond to cell entry values, exit values, and distance through the cell.
**2D Texture Map 1 (Approximation):** Stores dependencies of the volume rendering integral with respect to the length between two sample points, approximated in linear terms.
**2D Texture Map 2 (Residual):** Stores remaining parts of the integral that depend only on sample values.
**Projected Tetrahedra Geometry:** Each tetrahedron is decomposed into triangles.
Vertices are assigned all associated triangles.
**Pre-processing:** Compute the volume rendering integral for each cell.
*   If using 2D textures: Approximate dependencies on sample point distance linearly and store in the first 2D texture map.
**Decomposition:** Decompose each volume cell into tetrahedra, then into triangles.
**Projection:** Project the tetrahedra onto the screen.
*   Compute opacity and color at the thickest point for each tetrahedron.
*   Texture resolution: Not given in the sources.
*   **Approximation Error:** Linear approximation of integral dependencies may introduce errors for non-linear volume properties.
Sorts the cells before they are split into tetrahedra to ensure correct depth ordering.
Utilizes 2D texture mapping hardware to accelerate opacity interpolation and provide correct per-pixel opacity values.
**Time Complexity:** Pre-processing is required to compute texture maps.
Rendering time is reduced to texture lookups and compositing.
**Memory Complexity:** High for 3D texture approach; moderate for 2D texture approach.
**Strengths:** Supports arbitrary transfer functions (with 3D textures); leverages hardware texture interpolation.
**Limitations:** High memory consumption for 3D textures; 2D approximation limited to linear transfer functions; requires pre-processing.
**When to use:** When arbitrary transfer functions are needed and memory is sufficient, or when linear transfer functions are acceptable and memory is constrained.
**When not to use:** When memory is extremely limited and linear transfer functions are insufficient, or when dynamic transfer functions are required without pre-computation.
Originated with Röttger et al. [Röttger00], who introduced pre-integrated volume rendering for projected tetrahedra.
The method was extended by Guthe et al. [Guthe02] to add hardware-accelerated pre-integration [Engel01].
It builds on earlier parallel cell projection work by Lucas [Lucas92] and Stein et al. [243].
